message_1_subject: Mid-quarter check: OKR adjustments and QBR prep
message_1_body:
Team —

Quick mid-quarter pulse for Q2 OKRs. I pulled the latest tracker (attached) and flagged areas where we should consider scope adjustments or need dependency commitments ahead of the QBR. High level: overall plan is in decent shape but two KRs are at risk unless we get support on infra capacity and security evidence.

Snapshot (KR / owner / status / ask):
- Reduce inference P95 latency by 15% / Marcus / At risk — need final autoscale configs and a conservative capacity estimate (GPU slots + burst plan) by Friday EOD. See note in tab "Latency".
- Decrease per-token cost by 8% through batching and quantization / Marcus + Applied ML / On track — continue, but we should lock quantization profile for two top models.
- SLAs & compliance: SOC2 evidence, retention policy, and audit log export for Dedicated customers / Connor / At risk — Connor, can you confirm which artifacts we can include in the QBR pack and the ETA for the retention policy doc?
- Expansion: testbed with Tempo Labs (pilot) / Laura / At risk — they requested a short exec summary and top-line usage metrics for the pilot (see related_account).

Specific asks:
1) Marcus — send autoscale_capacity_estimate.pdf with 90/95 percentile traffic scenarios + cost delta by Friday so we can finalize the KR target. If we have to rescope, propose a narrowly reduced latency target that preserves user experience.
2) Connor — list of SOC2 artifacts we can present in the QBR and whether any evidence still needs remediation. If anything is blocked by legal, flag it.
3) Laura — own the QBR slide for "Production Economics" and confirm who will own the token-cost charts; I copied the QBR template for you to start with.

I want to avoid last-minute surprises in the QBR deck. If we need to re-scope any KR, call it out in your reply and include recommended wording and tradeoffs (customer impact, cost).

Attachment: Q2_OKR_tracker.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks —
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
message_2_subject: Re: Mid-quarter check: OKR adjustments and QBR prep
message_2_body:
Evelyn —

Thanks for the signal. Quick responses inline: 

- Autoscale/capacity: attaching a short PDF (autoscale_capacity_estimate.pdf) with 3 scenarios (conservative, expected, aggressive). For conservative we can meet ~10% P95 reduction with current infra + config changes; 15% will need either more reserved capacity (monthly commit) or enabling burst pools which increase cost by ~18%.

- Rescope proposal: if we can't get reserved capacity committed by next week, I propose changing the KR from 15% -> 12% P95 reduction and adding a sub-KR to reduce 99th percentile tail for high-cost requests. That keeps user experience intact and buys time for procurement. Draft wording below: 
  "Reduce inference P95 latency by 12% while decreasing burst cost by <=20%; implement tail-mitigation for top 5% of requests."

- Quantization: agree we should lock profiles for two models this sprint; scheduling a small rollout test on Thursday.

I'll finalize numbers and attach the PDF by EOD.

-Marcus
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
message_3_subject: Re: Mid-quarter check: OKR adjustments and QBR prep
message_3_body:
Evelyn / Team —

I'll take the QBR slide. I'll use QBR_input_template.docx and will populate the "Production Economics" slide with: current vs target P95, per-token unit cost trend (monthly), pilot usage (Tempo Labs), and any open risks. Need two quick confirmations: 

1) Who will own the per-route token-cost breakdown? Marcus?
2) Connor — can you give me the exact retention window and whether we can include sanitized audit logs in the pack by Tuesday so I can include a sample?

Deadline: I will circulate the first draft of slides Tuesday 6/23 10:00 PT so we can iterate before Friday leadership review.

Thanks —
Laura
Director, Customer Growth
